numerical_checks.result: 13 passed in 0.20 seconds: 10 aerial-productivity tests and 3 surface-comparison tests.
numerical_checks.coverage: Shared photon conservation, dark-body carbon failure, fixed renewal versus optional allocation, surface production at zero light, optical column mass independent of depth, exact stored-product regeneration, one shared phosphorus fallout credit, and rejection of communities with underfunded bottom layers.

review.activity: Substantive reading of the calculation and report, including separate reviews of light/carbon accounting and water, phosphorus and microbial interpretation.
findings_resolved: Phosphorus demand uses losses before atmospheric supply, so the shared fallout is credited only once.
A positive class-mean budget is insufficient for credited community production when a class bottom fails; both checks are required.
Water throughput retains the source's 1.83 kg C/m2/year assimilation basis; the concentrating trait's energy and combined physiology remain unresolved.
The microbial growth inputs are prescribed screening parameters, not measured airborne phototroph division rates.

The report distinguishes inherited diffuse-light canopy production from the new vertical-beam mutual-shading approximation. Existing angular tenant-light evidence is documented; no uncomputed diffuse-light production boost is added.
review.claim_limit: Numerical and substantive review does not establish empirical organism viability, a likely sky coverage, a maximum carrying capacity, or a coupled climate response. External-source access is recorded in sources.json; complete scholarly source review was not performed. The numerical1–5Gt C/year interval is not resolved for multiple scattering through the aerial community; a likely interval cannot be inferred from the prescribed cover and shadow cases.
